paragraph: Demarest's single-family market is the core of the town, with 32 sales over six months at a median of $1,687,500, and the typical sale is a five-bedroom colonial with three full baths. Sale prices ran from $785,000 to $4.6 million, so the median is the number to anchor on. With a sale-to-list ratio of essentially 1.00, about 34 percent of homes going above asking, and a median of 26.5 days on market, this is competitive but not frenzied. Well-priced homes are moving, and buyers should expect competition on the good ones. Townhouses, by contrast, are not the entry point here. All 10 sales were townhouses at a median of $2,365,000, four bedrooms and four baths, nothing above asking, and a median of 50.5 days on market. These are largely newer, larger units that trade at a premium to the average detached house, and sellers are okay with waiting for the right buyer. Closing volume built steadily into midsummer, with 12 single-family sales in July, so the town is tracking the normal seasonal arc; monthly medians swing hard because several months had fewer than five closings, and they should not be read as price moves. If you're weighing the two tiers, the deciding factor isn't market heat. It's whether you want the space and grounds of a single-family or the low-maintenance setup of a newer townhouse at a similar or higher price.
